v.rationale:
I reviewed impl-2 first, then impl-1. Both pass all their tests (impl-2: 16, impl-1: 24) and their code is very similar. Both use the same scheduler settings: onOneServer, withoutOverlapping with a sized expiry, and Copenhagen timezone. Both use the same unique-job setup with UniqueFor under one hour, Tries(1), Timeout(2700) and FailOnTimeout, and both delete carts in batches by id. My probes showed both prune schedules are due on both DST days. Both also schedule the hourly sync correctly.

The difference is where the long connection is set. impl-1 binds SyncSupplierStock to its long connection with a #[Connection] attribute on the job, which Bus\Dispatcher reads, so every dispatch gets the longer retry_after. impl-2 sets the connection only on the Schedule::job call. A manual dispatch in impl-2 goes to the default redis connection, where retry_after is 90 seconds against a 2700-second timeout. A slow run would then be picked up by a second worker and run twice, which is the kind of double run the task forbids. impl-1's tests are also much stronger. They check Copenhagen local time with isDue() in winter and summer, against UTC and on a wrong day. They also show that two schedule:run calls dispatch once, test the UniqueLock and test the mail rendering. impl-2 has a placeholder expect(true) test and a de-duplication test that dispatches only once. impl-2 is slightly leaner, but impl-1 is more robust and better tested, so impl-1 ranks first.
